description: ADJ-LADDER rung 7 — evidence-based-medicine effect measures (ARR / RR / RRR) computed from two stated event rates. A NEW reasoning kind: biostatistics. Each item is a compute_dimensioned program (observe the two rates, let answer = formula); the ADJ engine carries the arithmetic and the harness matches the scalar to the printed options. Contamination-safe: the only literals are the two stated rates (no structural constants). The five options are the five natural quantities {ARR, RR, RRR, CER, EER}, so the distractors are exactly the measures students confuse.

items.stem: In a randomized trial the event rate was 0.4 in the control group and 0.1 in the treated group. What is the absolute risk reduction (ARR)?
items.program:
observe control(0.4)
observe treated(0.1)
let answer = control - treated
? answer

items.stem: In a randomized trial the event rate was 0.4 in the control group and 0.1 in the treated group. What is the relative risk (RR) of the treated group versus control?
items.program:
observe control(0.4)
observe treated(0.1)
let answer = treated / control
? answer

items.stem: In a randomized trial the event rate was 0.4 in the control group and 0.1 in the treated group. What is the relative risk reduction (RRR)?
items.program:
observe control(0.4)
observe treated(0.1)
let answer = (control - treated) / control
? answer
